notes: Prior finding l1-run4-001 VERIFIED RESOLVED: the amended 5.1 rule 2 text (and its echoes at section 7 constraint 1 and section 11 note 4, both re-read) describes the shipped sanitizeTrackingValue accurately -- .slice(0, 255), then drop of a trailing code unit in 0xD800-0xDBFF, 254 units when the slice splits a pair, with the same Rails-json-rejection rationale the code comment gives. One precision point checked and settled in the code's favor: the code's drop condition is the trailing-unit range check alone, while the spec's provenance clause says 'left when the slice splits a surrogate pair' -- these are observationally identical on the declared input domain, because location.search is a USVString (lone surrogates are replaced with U+FFFD by the browser before the string exists) and both decodeURIComponent and the installed decode-uri-component 0.2.0 fallback (read in full) never synthesize a lone surrogate from percent tokens (CESU-8 surrogate sequences throw and are left as literal text), so the slice is the only producer of a trailing lone high surrogate reachable through the helper; divergence exists only for hand-crafted direct calls with malformed strings, the same degenerate-direct-call class as the settled-LOW 'sanitizer throw on non-string input'. Also checked: empty-string values survive as '' (charCodeAt(-1) is NaN, range check false); repeated-param first-occurrence semantics are literal (a first occurrence that parsed to null is kept as null); a literal ?utm_data=x URL param lands inside utmData under key 'utm_data' per the spec's literal every-other-utm_-param rule.
